title: The Woman Who Made Me Walk Away
content: Diane—my wife—she looked at me one night and said, 'Peter, the grandkids should know you as more than a voice on the phone.' That's when I knew. I was still running models at all hours, still checking backtests on vacation. I walked away at fifty-eight. Best investment I ever made.
extended_content: We met in a statistics class at URI. She got the better grade, and she's never needed to remind me. When Danny and Kate were little I missed too much. Kate's school play? Diane told me about it. Danny's science fair? I made it—barely—and took a call in the hallway. Diane never complained, which made it worse. I told myself I'd do better with the grandkids, and then I caught myself doing the exact same thing. That's when she said it plainly. You can always run another model. You can't get another Saturday with a six-year-old. She was right. She's usually right. People thought I was crazy to leave. Best decision I ever made.
when_to_tell: when someone is struggling with work-life balance or priorities
lesson: Some investments don't show up in financial statements. Family is the most important portfolio.
